ADA-2026-DX.text: Prediabetes: FPG 5.6–6.9 mmol/L (100–125 mg/dL); diabetes: FPG ≥7.0 mmol/L (≥126 mg/dL)

ADA-2026-PREV.text: Prediabetes: weight reduction of at least 5–7% and ≥150 min/week moderate-intensity physical activity

BCAA-T2D.text: Branched-chain amino acids (NMR) predicted type 2 diabetes, OR 1.31–1.33 per SD after adjusting for BMI and fasting glucose (young Finns, n=11,896)

CFDNA-FRAGMENTOMICS-SEQ.text: Validated fragmentomics cancer detection (DELFI) uses low-coverage whole-genome sequencing (1–2×), not capillary electrophoresis. A Thai CE-feature + AFP machine-learning study for liver-cancer surveillance (n=69 external validation, AUC 0.93) is single-centre research without regulatory clearance; no validated CE-only multi-cancer screening method was found
CFDNA-FRAGMENTOMICS-SEQ.source: Cristiano S et al. Nature 2019; CEliver, Communications Medicine 2026

ESC-2021-DIET.text: Adopting a Mediterranean or similar diet is recommended to lower the risk of cardiovascular disease (more vegetables, fruit, whole grains, legumes, nuts, fish and olive oil; less red/processed meat and sugar)
ESC-2021-DIET.source: 2021 ESC Guidelines on cardiovascular disease prevention in clinical practice

FIB4-MASLD.text: FIB-4 = age × AST / (platelets [10^9/L] × √ALT). Below 1.3 low risk of advanced fibrosis (re-assess every 1–3 years); 1.3–2.67 intermediate; above 2.67 high; in people older than 65 the lower cut-off is 2.0
FIB4-MASLD.source: EASL-EASD-EASO Clinical Practice Guidelines on MASLD 2024

FLI-2006.text: Fatty Liver Index = e^y/(1+e^y) × 100, y = 0.953·ln(TG mg/dL) + 0.139·BMI + 0.718·ln(GGT U/L) + 0.053·waist(cm) − 15.745; FLI <30 rules out (LR− 0.2), ≥60 rules in fatty liver (LR+ 4.3). Developed in an Italian cohort
FLI-2006.source: Bedogni G et al. BMC Gastroenterology 2006;6:33

METS-HARMONIZED-2009.text: Harmonized metabolic syndrome: ≥3 of 5 — waist (Asian ≥90 cm men / ≥80 cm women), TG ≥150 mg/dL or treatment, HDL <40 (men) / <50 (women) mg/dL or treatment, BP ≥130/85 or treatment, fasting glucose ≥100 mg/dL or treatment
METS-HARMONIZED-2009.source: Alberti KGMM et al. Circulation 2009;120:1640 (thresholds confirmed from abstract and secondary sources; original Table 1 not opened)

OTVOS-2011-DISCORDANCE.text: MESA (n=6,814): when LDL-C and LDL-P are discordant, only LDL-P predicted CVD (HR 1.45 per SD vs 1.07)
OTVOS-2011-DISCORDANCE.source: Otvos JD et al. J Clin Lipidol 2011

RCPT-2024-DIET.text: High LDL-C: saturated fat <7% of daily energy, replace with unsaturated oils, avoid trans fat, more fibre

RCPT-2024-FOLLOWUP.text: Follow-up lipid test within 4–12 weeks after starting a statin to evaluate effectiveness and assess adherence

RCPT-2024-SMOKING.text: Quit smoking or refer to a smoking cessation clinic
RCPT-2024-SMOKING.source: RCPT dyslipidemia guideline 2024; Thai Hypertension guideline 2024

RCPT-2024-TG.text: High TG: abstain from alcohol, reduce carbohydrate, sugar <10% of energy

TCVRS-2021.text: Thai CV Risk Score 2.5 (Rama-EGAT): 10-year CVD risk; <10% low, 10–<20% moderate, 20–30% high, >30% very high

TDRS-2006.text: Thai diabetes risk score (0–17). ≥6 = high risk, add blood glucose test (sens 77%, spec 60%, AUC 0.74)
TDRS-2006.source: Aekplakorn W et al. Diabetes Care 2006;29:1872

THAI-HT-2024-NA.text: Sodium no more than 2 g/day (≈1 tsp salt or 3 tsp fish sauce/soy sauce)

THAI-OBESITY.text: Thai normal BMI 18.5–22.9; obesity BMI ≥25 and/or waist ≥90 cm (men) / ≥80 cm (women) or waist > height/2
THAI-OBESITY.source: Thai Hypertension guideline 2024; Diabetes Association of Thailand

WHO-2005-PREVENTABLE.text: If the major risk factors for chronic disease were eliminated, at least 80% of heart disease, stroke and type 2 diabetes would be prevented; and 40% of cancer would be prevented
WHO-2005-PREVENTABLE.source: WHO 2005, Preventing chronic diseases: a vital investment (wording from secondary copies; WHO PDF not opened)

WHO-PA-2020.text: Adults: 150–300 min/week moderate or 75–150 min/week vigorous aerobic activity + muscle strengthening ≥2 days/week
WHO-PA-2020.source: WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour 2020

WHO-SEDENTARY-2020.text: Adults should limit the amount of time spent being sedentary; replacing sedentary time with physical activity of any intensity (including light intensity) provides health benefits
WHO-SEDENTARY-2020.source: WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour 2020
